reproduction_target: Production of the telomere-to-telomere, chromosome-level annotated reference genome rPleFas1.1 of Plestiodon fasciatus: (1) RNA-seq QC and adapter trimming (FastQC, Trimmomatic defaults), (2) PacBio HiFi de novo draft assembly with Hifiasm v0.25.0 run without Hi-C reads, (3) soft-masking of the draft with the EarlGrey v4.1.1 pipeline prior to Hi-C mapping, (4) Hi-C incorporation via BWA v0.7.19 alignment, SAMtools v1.22.1 duplicate removal, YAHS v1.2.2 scaffolding, Juicer Tools contact-map generation and Juicebox Assembly Tools v2.20.0 visualisation, (5) telomere confirmation with tidk v0.2.65 plus GC-content inspection, (6) TE modelling and quantification with EarlGrey v4.1.1 on the final assembly, (7) functional gene annotation through the funannotate train/predict/update/fix/annotate pipeline (Trinity, PASA, Augustus, EvidenceModeler, BUSCO tetrapoda with Taeniopygia guttata seed) with InterProScan v5.74-105.0 and eggNOG-mapper v2.1.12 evidence, (8) re-running the same annotation pipeline on four previously published skink assemblies for comparative TE analysis, (9) BUSCO/compleasm completeness assessment and BUSCO-gene synteny plotting across six skink genomes with the authors' custom Synk tool plus RIdeogram, (10) an inconclusive FindZX sex-linked-region scan, and (11) the Circos ideogram of Figure 1. Field collection, euthanasia, tissue preservation, RNA/DNA extraction, PacBio Revio HiFi sequencing and Phase Genomics Proximo Hi-C library construction are upstream wet-lab work recorded as W (OOS).

steps.label: Initial quality check of the six-tissue Illumina NovaSeq 2x150bp poly(A) RNA-seq libraries with FastQC (cited to Brown et al. 2017 / FQC Dashboard). No FastQC version, no invocation, no report deposited; the prose only asserts that 'all RNA sequences passed the initial quality check'

Adapter filtering and trimming of the RNA-seq reads with Trimmomatic 'using the default settings' (Bolger et al. 2014). Defaults are stated, but no version is given and no Trimmomatic command appears in either deposited repository; note that the funannotate train step in the Genome-Annotation repo is explicitly run on UNTRIMMED reads, so the prose and the deposited scripts disagree about whether trimmed reads entered the annotation

De novo haplotype-resolved draft assembly of the PacBio Revio HiFi reads with Hifiasm v0.25.0 (Cheng et al. 2021), deliberately run WITHOUT the Hi-C reads because their inclusion inflated the contig count from 34 to ~6,000. Version exactly pinned in prose; the verbatim SLURM script ('hifiasm -o hoff_hifi_assembly.asm -l 2 -t 32 <hifi_reads.fastq>') is public, but in the jomhoff/Genome-Assembly repository, which the paper's Data Availability statement does NOT cite - it is reachable only via a link inside pipeline.md of the cited assembly repo

Soft-masking of the Hifiasm draft assembly with the EarlGrey v4.1.1 pipeline (Baril et al. 2024) prior to Hi-C mapping, run with default settings. Version exactly pinned; the verbatim SLURM script ('earlGrey -g $genome -s plestiodonFasciatus_2 -t $SLURM_NTASKS_PER_NODE -d yes -o ./earlgreyOutputs') is in the cited Genome-Annotation repo. Input is the undeposited draft assembly, an intermediate regenerable from C3

Alignment of the Phase Genomics Hi-C read pairs to the soft-masked HiFi draft with BWA v0.7.19 (Li 2013). Version exactly pinned in prose; the deposited pipeline.md gives the index step and the exact mem invocation ('bwa mem -t 25 -5SP $DRAFT $HICR1 $HICR2 | samtools view -bS -'). Input Hi-C FASTQs are referenced by absolute cluster path in the script; the raw reads are covered by BioProject PRJNA1278702 but the script cannot be run as written

Post-alignment processing with SAMtools v1.22.1 (Danecek et al. 2021) to name-sort, fixmate, coordinate-sort, index, markdup -r (remove duplicates) and re-name-sort for YAHS. Version exactly pinned; the full six-command sequence with thread counts is deposited verbatim in pipeline.md

Hi-C scaffolding of the draft assembly with the de novo YAHS v1.2.2 pipeline (Zhou et al. 2023), producing the chromosome-level assembly with 18 unplaced scaffolds. Version exactly pinned in prose and a SLURM script is present in pipeline.md, but the Methods text states no YAHS arguments (resolution schedule, restriction-enzyme motif, no-contig-error-correction flags), so the parameter record rests entirely on the undocumented script body

Generation of the Hi-C contact map with Juicer Tools (Durand et al. 2016). No version at all (Juicer Tools 1.x vs 2.x differ materially), no subcommand named, no resolution list, no assembly-to-.hic conversion parameters stated in the Methods

Visualisation (and implicit manual review) of the chromosome-level scaffolding in Juicebox Assembly Tools v2.20.0 (Robinson et al. 2018). Version exactly pinned, but this is an interactive GUI step: no record of whether any manual joins/breaks were applied, no .assembly review file deposited, no decision criteria stated

Telomere confirmation across the complete autosomal genome with tidk v0.2.65 (Brown et al. 2025), which outputs counts of telomeric repeats in windows. Version exactly pinned, but no subcommand (search vs explore vs find), no telomeric repeat motif, no window size, and no tidk invocation appears in either deposited repository

TE modelling, quantification and soft-masking of the FINAL chromosome-level assembly with EarlGrey v4.1.1 (Baril et al. 2024) using default settings, explicitly including a 100bp minimum length and 10 iterations of the BLAST-extract-extend process; produces the 46.7% repeat estimate and the Kimura 2-parameter divergence landscape of Figure 2. Version exactly pinned, defaults and the two non-default-relevant settings stated, script deposited. The underlying Dfam/RepBase library version consumed by EarlGrey is not recorded anywhere

funannotate 'train' step: aligns the six-tissue RNA-seq, assembles with Trinity (Grabherr et al. 2011) and runs PASA (Haas et al. 2003) to model gene structures. The deposited script gives the full command line (--max_intronlen 6000 --stranded RF, all twelve FASTQ files listed), but NO version is given in the Methods for funannotate itself (v1.8.1 appears only as the bibliography entry for Palmer & Stajich 2020), nor for Trinity or PASA, and the funannotate_db and GENEMARK_PATH are absolute cluster paths with no database release recorded

funannotate 'predict' step: PASA gene models train Augustus (Stanke et al. 2008) before EvidenceModeler (Haas et al. 2008) is run, with the Tetrapoda BUSCO database and Taeniopygia guttata as seed species, --organism other and --repeats2evm. Command line deposited and options stated, but no version for funannotate, Augustus, EvidenceModeler, GeneMark-ES (installed separately from topaz.gatech.edu, a licence-gated download) or the Tetrapoda BUSCO/odb release

funannotate 'update' and 'fix' steps: UTR addition and correction of gene models that disagree with the RNA-seq evidence. The 'update' command is deposited; the 'fix' step is described in prose only ('which are corrected in the fix step') with no command, no manual-curation record of which models were fixed, and no version

InterProScan v5.74-105.0 (Jones et al. 2014) run against the InterPro database for gene families, ahead of the funannotate 'annotate' step. Version exactly pinned including the data release suffix (105.0), and the repo ships an interproscan.properties configuration file. No invocation flags (applications enabled, -goterms, -pa) are given in the Methods

eggNOG-mapper v2.1.12 (Cantalapiedra et al. 2021) downloaded locally and executed during the funannotate 'annotate' step. Tool version exactly pinned, but the eggNOG DATABASE release (5.0.2 vs 6) is not stated, nor are the search mode (diamond/mmseqs), tax_scope, or e-value cutoffs

funannotate 'annotate' step incorporating the InterProScan and eggNOG-mapper evidence, using 'the default functional annotation databases' (Pfam, MEROPS, CAZyme, BUSCO, GO, UniProt/Swiss-Prot). Produces the headline 32,520 predicted protein-coding genes and 16,100 uniquely named genes. No funannotate version, and 'default databases' is recorded without a single database release identifier or download date, so the annotation cannot be re-derived to the same content

Re-running the entire EarlGrey + funannotate pipeline on four previously published chromosome-level skink assemblies (Tiliqua scincoides, Spondylurus nitidus, Bassiana duperreyi, Carinascincus ocellatus) to produce the comparative TE-composition and Kimura-divergence panels of Figure 2. The four input assemblies are given as species names only - NO accession, NO assembly version, NO download date - and no comparative driver script is deposited; the RNA-seq evidence status for these four species is not stated

compleasm (Huang & Li 2023) run to extract single-copy BUSCO gene coordinates for each of the six skink assemblies, as the input stage of the Synk synteny pipeline. No compleasm version and no lineage/odb release stated in the Methods; the Synk repository's environment.yml specifies only a floating 'compleasm>=0.2.8' with no lock

Synteny plotting between P. fasciatus and Bassiana duperreyi, Spondylurus nitidus, Carinascincus ocellatus, Tiliqua scincoides and P. gilberti with the authors' custom Synk tool (https://github.com/jomhoff/Synk), which isolates BUSCO genes into comparative text files and calls RIdeogram (Hao et al. 2020) in one script. The repository is public and MIT-licensed but carries NO release tag and NO commit is cited; its last push (2026-07-15) post-dates the v2 preprint (2025-11-14) and the README documents a '--reuse_compleasm' one-shot wrapper interface that did not exist at publication, so the deposited code has demonstrably drifted from the code that produced Figure 3. No RIdeogram version, no karyotype/replacement files deposited

BUSCO completeness assessment of the final assembly reported in the Abstract and Table 1 (98% of 7,480 BUSCO markers, lineage Sauropsida). The Methods never name the tool that produced this number (BUSCO proper or compleasm), give no version, no odb release, and no mode (genome vs protein)

Attempted identification of sex-linked regions with the FindZX pipeline (Sigeman et al. 2022) using two male and two female P. fasciatus; reported verbatim as 'the results were inconclusive'. Blocked on every axis: the four resequenced individuals are named nowhere, have no accession and are absent from the Data Availability statement and from BioProject PRJNA1278702 as described; no FindZX version, no snakemake config, no reference/window settings, and no output is shown

Figure 1 ideogram plotted with Circos (Krzywinski et al. 2009): chromosome sizes, 50kb-window gene-density heatmap, 50kb-window repeat-element heatmap and a GC-content line chart. Window size is stated, but no Circos version, no karyotype/configuration files, no data-track derivation scripts (how gene and repeat density per 50kb were computed) are deposited or described

Field collection of an adult female Plestiodon fasciatus in Allegan County, Michigan (42.5394, -85.9949) under Michigan DNR permits and AMNH IACUC protocols, euthanasia with MS-222, and sampling of liver, lung, heart, skeletal muscle, kidney and skin into NAP buffer (Camacho-Sanchez et al. 2013) for RNA preservation. Vouchered as AMNH-179334

Field collection of a second adult female P. fasciatus in McCracken County, Kentucky (37.1501, -88.7953) under Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife permits, providing a whole-blood sample stored in EDTA, after the PacBio Revio effort on the NAP-preserved Michigan liver proved suboptimal. Vouchered as AMNH-179327. The genome and the transcriptome therefore come from two different individuals ~650km apart

RNA extraction, poly(A)-selected strand-specific mRNA library preparation and Illumina NovaSeq 2x150bp sequencing of the six Michigan tissues at Azenta/Genewiz, generating ~100M paired-end reads. Kit, protocol version and lot numbers are not given (vendor service)

High-molecular-weight genomic DNA extraction from the EDTA blood of AMNH-179327 with the Qiagen MagAttract HMW DNA kit, following the 'Manual Purification of High-Molecular-Weight Genomic DNA from Whole Blood' protocol of the MagAttract HMW DNA Handbook, performed in the AMNH Institute for Comparative Genomics. Protocol named but handbook revision not cited

PacBio Revio HiFi sequencing of the extracted gDNA on 1 SMRT cell at Azenta/Genewiz, yielding ~6.3 million read pairs, ~79GB, mean read length ~12,000bp and ~53x coverage against an estimated 1.5GB genome. Chemistry version, SMRT Link version and CCS settings not stated

Hi-C chromatin-interaction library construction from a blood sample on the Phase Genomics Proximo animal genome scaffolding platform and Illumina NovaSeq 2x150bp sequencing, generating 300 million read pairs of which 56% were high quality and 1,721,863 per contig were 'usable' (mapping to different >5kb contigs). Restriction enzyme(s) used by Proximo are not named, which also leaves the YAHS enzyme parameter undeterminable from the paper

headline.static_readiness: 0/23 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on 8/23 computational steps (35%). This paper is unusual among the genome-resource cohort in that the CODE axis is comparatively strong and the VERSION axis is what binds. Three public MIT-licensed GitHub repositories exist (jomhoff/Chromosome-level_genome_assembly, jomhoff/Genome-Annotation, both cited in Data Availability, plus jomhoff/Synk cited inline in the Synteny analysis subsection), and a fourth (jomhoff/Genome-Assembly) is reachable only through a link inside pipeline.md. Between them they ship verbatim SLURM submission scripts with real command lines for hifiasm, EarlGrey, BWA, SAMtools, YAHS and the four funannotate sub-steps, which is materially better than prose-only reconstruction and is why 11 steps reach code = 2. The version axis then caps everything at 1: nine tools are exactly pinned in prose (Hifiasm v0.25.0, EarlGrey v4.1.1, BWA v0.7.19, SAMtools v1.22.1, YAHS v1.2.2, Juicebox Assembly Tools v2.20.0, tidk v0.2.65, InterProScan v5.74-105.0, eggNOG-mapper v2.1.12) and those pins produce exactly the 8 RI steps, but there is NO environment closure anywhere: the deposited scripts activate named conda/mamba environments by absolute cluster path ('conda activate /mendel-nas1/jhoffman1/miniforge3/envs/hic', 'mamba activate funannotate', 'conda activate fasciatus_ass') and no environment export, lockfile, container image or module list is provided for any of them, so capture_claim is exact_pins_partial and version stays at 1 wherever it is credited. 14/23 steps fall to NI, almost all on version = 0: the entire read-QC front end (FastQC, Trimmomatic - both unversioned despite defaults being declared), Juicer Tools (no version at all, and Juicer Tools 1.x vs 2.x are not interchangeable), the whole funannotate stack (funannotate itself, Trinity, PASA, Augustus, EvidenceModeler and GeneMark-ES are all unversioned - v1.8.1 appears only as a bibliography entry, never as a Methods claim), compleasm, RIdeogram, Circos and Synk. A second, distinct defect runs through the annotation half: reference-database releases are never recorded. 'the default functional annotation databases', the Tetrapoda BUSCO set, the InterPro data release beyond the 105.0 suffix, the eggNOG database release and the Dfam/RepBase library consumed by EarlGrey are all unversioned, so the 32,520-gene and 16,100-named-gene headline numbers are not re-derivable even with the exact tool versions. 1/23 is blocked (X): the FindZX sex-linked-region scan used two male and two female P. fasciatus whose sequence data are named nowhere, accessioned nowhere and absent from the Data Availability statement. Finally, a code-drift finding that only a landing-page read can catch: the Synk repository's last push (2026-07-15) post-dates the v2 preprint (2025-11-14) and its README now documents a one-shot compleasm wrapper interface that cannot have been the interface used for Figure 3, and no tag or commit hash is cited to recover the published state - none of the four repositories carries a single release or tag. Note the Delta-5 symmetry caveat: a 0 static_readiness under-claims by construction, because Tier-1 cannot credit an undeclared-but-present dependency specification.
headline.coverage: 23 computational steps and 6 wet-lab steps assessed from the bioRxiv v2 JATS full text (Abstract; Materials & Methods subsections 'Sample Acquisition', 'RNA extraction and sequencing', 'Genomic DNA extraction and sequencing', 'Draft Genome assembly', 'Hi-C incorporation', 'TE and gene annotation', 'Synteny analysis'; Results and Discussion; Data availability) plus the landing pages and README/pipeline prose of the four author repositories (jomhoff/Chromosome-level_genome_assembly, jomhoff/Genome-Annotation, jomhoff/Synk, jomhoff/Genome-Assembly). Computational coverage |S|/(|S|+|W|) = 23/29 = 79%. This is a genome-resource paper: field collection, euthanasia, tissue preservation, HMW DNA extraction, PacBio Revio sequencing and Phase Genomics Proximo Hi-C are load-bearing and irreproducible by construction; the computational reproduction entry point is the raw data under BioProject PRJNA1278702 plus the Figshare project.

gaps.where: The whole toolchain (all 23 computational steps); version = 0 specifically at C1, C2, C8, C12, C13, C14, C17, C18, C19, C20, C21, C22, C23
gaps.missing: Two distinct version defects. (a) No version at all for FastQC, Trimmomatic, Juicer Tools, funannotate, Trinity, PASA, Augustus, EvidenceModeler, GeneMark-ES, compleasm, RIdeogram, Circos, FindZX or the authors' own Synk tool. funannotate 'v1.8.1' appears only inside the Palmer & Stajich (2020) bibliography entry, never as a claim about what was run. (b) No environment closure of any kind anywhere: the deposited SLURM scripts activate named conda/mamba environments by absolute cluster path ('conda activate /mendel-nas1/jhoffman1/miniforge3/envs/hic', 'mamba activate earlgrey', 'mamba activate funannotate', 'conda activate fasciatus_ass') and no environment.yml export, conda-lock, pixi lock, container image or HPC module list accompanies any of them. The nine exact prose pins (Hifiasm 0.25.0, EarlGrey 4.1.1, BWA 0.7.19, SAMtools 1.22.1, YAHS 1.2.2, Juicebox 2.20.0, tidk 0.2.65, InterProScan 5.74-105.0, eggNOG-mapper 2.1.12) therefore have no dependency closure behind them, so capture_claim is exact_pins_partial and version is capped at 1.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a versions table naming an exact version for every tool invoked, and export the four cluster conda/mamba environments to lockfiles (conda-lock or an explicit-spec `conda list --explicit`) committed alongside the scripts that activate them, or ship a container digest covering the assembly and the annotation toolchains separately.

gaps.where: C11, C12, C13, C15, C16, C17, C18, C19, C21 - every database-consuming annotation and completeness step
gaps.missing: No reference-database release is recorded anywhere. The funannotate 'annotate' step is described only as using 'the default functional annotation databases'; the Tetrapoda BUSCO database used as the predict-step training set has no odb release; the Sauropsida BUSCO set behind the headline '98% of 7,480 markers' has no release; the eggNOG database release consumed by eggNOG-mapper v2.1.12 is not stated (only the mapper version); the Dfam/RepBase TE library consumed by EarlGrey v4.1.1 is not stated; the InterPro data release is implicit in the '105.0' suffix but no download date is given; and FUNANNOTATE_DB is an absolute cluster path with no manifest. These databases are the direct determinants of the 32,520-gene / 16,100-named-gene headline result and of the 46.7% repeat fraction.
gaps.how_to_close: Record the release identifier and download date of every consumed database (funannotate_db manifest, BUSCO/odb release, eggNOG DB release, Dfam/RepBase version, InterPro data release) and, better, deposit the database manifests or their checksums with the pipeline repositories.

gaps.where: All four repositories: jomhoff/Chromosome-level_genome_assembly, jomhoff/Genome-Annotation, jomhoff/Synk, jomhoff/Genome-Assembly; sharpest at C20 (Synk)
gaps.missing: The deposited code is real and useful but is not citable at a fixed state. None of the four repositories carries a single release or tag (tags=0, releases=0 on all four as of 2026-07-27), no commit hash is cited in the paper, and none is archived to Zenodo or Software Heritage, so there is no DOI and no immutable snapshot. The drift is not hypothetical: jomhoff/Synk was last pushed 2026-07-15, eight months after the v2 preprint (2025-11-14), and its current README documents a one-shot compleasm wrapper ('python synk.py --main_name pfas --main_assembly pfas.fa --compare NAME=ASSEMBLY ... --reuse_compleasm') that cannot be the interface used to produce Figure 3. A reader today cannot recover the code that made the published figure. Separately, jomhoff/Genome-Assembly - which contains the actual hifiasm command line for the paper's central assembly step - is NOT cited in the Data Availability statement at all and is reachable only via a hyperlink buried in pipeline.md of a different repository.
gaps.how_to_close: Tag a release in each of the four repositories at the state that produced the published results, archive each to Zenodo for a versioned DOI, cite those DOIs in the Data Availability statement, and add jomhoff/Genome-Assembly to that statement explicitly.

gaps.missing: The sex-linked-region analysis used whole-genome data from two male and two female P. fasciatus. These four individuals are given no catalogue numbers, no accessions and no BioSample identifiers, they are not mentioned in the Data availability statement, and they are not described in any Methods subsection - the sequencing of the four is never reported. No FindZX version, no snakemake configuration and no output are shown; the result is dismissed in one clause as 'inconclusive'.
gaps.how_to_close: Either accession and describe the four resequenced individuals with the FindZX configuration and its output, or remove the claim; an inconclusive result reported without its inputs is not assessable.

gaps.where: C5, C6, C7, C12, C13, C14 - every deposited SLURM script
gaps.missing: The deposited scripts are environment-hardcoded transcripts rather than runnable artefacts. Inputs, outputs and databases are absolute paths on the AMNH mendel cluster (/home/jhoffman1/mendel-nas1/..., /mendel-nas1/jhoffman1/miniforge3/envs/...), the GeneMark installation is a hand-placed directory (gmes_linux_64_4) from a licence-gated download at topaz.gatech.edu, thread counts are taken from $SLURM_NTASKS_PER_NODE with node-specific #SBATCH resource requests, and there is no driver, no config file and no parameterisation. Nothing in the repositories can be executed by a reader without rewriting every path.
gaps.how_to_close: Parameterise the scripts (config file or command-line arguments for input/output/database paths), or wrap the pipeline in Snakemake/Nextflow with a profile, so that the deposited code is executable rather than illustrative.

gaps.where: C4, C5, C6, C7, C9, C13, C14, C15, C16, C17, C19, C20, C23 - all intermediates
gaps.missing: Only the final assembly and the raw reads are deposited. The Hifiasm draft assembly (hoff_pfas_total.fasta), the EarlGrey soft-masked draft, the Hi-C alignment BAMs, the YAHS scaffolding output and .hic contact map, the Juicebox review file, the funannotate train/predict/update intermediates, the compleasm full_table outputs and the Synk karyotype/replacement files are all undeposited. Each is in principle regenerable from C3 onwards, but every regeneration inherits the version and database gaps above, so the annotation intermediates in particular are not recoverable to the same content. The Figshare project is cited only as a bare project URL with no item list, so what it contains cannot be determined from the paper.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the draft assembly, the soft-masked genome, the .hic contact map and the final GFF3/protein FASTA as itemised, individually-cited Figshare or NCBI records rather than an unenumerated project link.

gaps.missing: Two interactive/undocumented curation points sit on the critical path. Juicebox Assembly Tools v2.20.0 is described as being used to 'visualize the scaffolding', but Juicebox Assembly Tools is a manual curation environment and the paper does not state whether any joins, breaks or inversions were applied by hand, nor is any .assembly or .review file deposited - so it is unknown whether the published chromosome-level assembly is the unmodified YAHS output. The funannotate 'fix' step is likewise described in one clause with no command, no list of corrected models and no criteria.
gaps.how_to_close: State explicitly whether manual curation was applied in Juicebox and deposit the .assembly/.review file if so; deposit the funannotate fix command and the list of corrected gene models.

gaps.missing: The Methods state that sequencing adapters were 'filtered and trimmed with trimmomatic using the default settings' before use, but the deposited functional_annotation.md explicitly says 'I initiate the step with untrimmed RNA-seq data' and the funannotate train command lists the raw *_R1_001.fastq.gz / *_R2_001.fastq.gz files. The prose and the deposited code disagree about which RNA-seq reads entered the annotation that produced the paper's headline gene counts.
gaps.how_to_close: Reconcile the text with the deposited script - state which read set was actually used for the funannotate train step, and if both were tried, report which produced the published annotation.

gaps.where: C18 (comparative re-run on four skink assemblies)
gaps.missing: The four comparison genomes (Tiliqua scincoides, Spondylurus nitidus, Bassiana duperreyi, Carinascincus ocellatus) that underpin the paper's central comparative claim - that TE amount and content are 'remarkably conserved across Scincidae' - are identified by species name only. No GCA/GCF accession, no assembly version, no download date, no source. The same is true of the P. gilberti assembly used in the synteny comparison (Figure 3). The species names are also inconsistently spelled across the text ('Carinascincus occelatus' vs 'ocellatus', 'Tiliqua scinciodes' vs 'scincoides'), which blocks even name-based lookup.
gaps.how_to_close: Give the versioned assembly accession (GCA_/GCF_ with version suffix) and access date for each of the five external genomes used in the comparative TE and synteny analyses.

gaps.missing: GeneMark-ES is licence-gated: the deposited script sets GENEMARK_PATH to a hand-installed gmes_linux_64_4 directory and functional_annotation.md instructs the reader to 'install GeneMark separately' from topaz.gatech.edu, which requires accepting an academic licence and issues a time-limited key. No version of the GeneMark release is recorded, and the gene-prediction step cannot be run without a separately obtained, expiring credential.
gaps.how_to_close: Record the exact GeneMark-ES/ET release used, and report whether an alternative open predictor was evaluated, so that readers without a current GeneMark key can assess the impact.
